rules.title: `Core\Cli::arguments` is how a program reads the words it was started with, at every depth
rules.divergesFromPhp: `$argv` and `$argc` do not exist, the elements are `tainted`, and the answer is a process fact rather than a per-isolate one

rules.title: `Core\Script::args` is the value the current isolate was spawned with, and `null` where there was none
rules.divergesFromPhp: Novis's own `$_ARGS` superglobal was retired for the same reason PHP's were — a spawned isolate reads its argument through a member

rules.title: `Core\Process` is the one way to run another program, and there is no shell string anywhere in it
rules.divergesFromPhp: `exec`, `system`, `shell_exec`, `passthru`, `popen`, `proc_open` and backticks are all gone, and no flag brings a command line back

rules.title: `run` waits by suspending the coroutine, and hands back the exit code with both captures as `bytes`
rules.divergesFromPhp: captured output is `bytes`, so text costs an `as string` that throws on invalid UTF-8 rather than mangling it

rules.title: `ProcessOptions` carries a working directory, a replaced environment and a timeout, and nothing else
rules.divergesFromPhp: a supplied environment replaces the parent's rather than merging with it

rules.title: `spawn` answers a handle whose reads and writes suspend, covering `proc_open` and `passthru` in one type
A target only a second command-line parser could run is refused, on every platform
rules.divergesFromPhp: a `.bat`, `.cmd` or `.ps1` target does not run at all; a shebang script does, because `execve` reads it without re-parsing anything

rules.title: `Core\IO::writeStream` is where every stream reaches disk, and a failed write removes its partial file
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `move_uploaded_file` and no temp file to move — a part is streamed to a path the program chose, and `overwrite` defaults to false

rules.title: A temporary directory lives under a Novis-owned root and is deleted when its script ends, and the sweep never throws
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `tmpfile`, no `sys_get_temp_dir` writing and no `tempnam` — the runtime hands out a directory it owns and reclaims it

rules.title: The orphan sweep is keyed on the owner being alive, never on age, and runs in exactly two places
A pattern runs on the linear engine unless it cannot, and the backtracking tier's step budget throws when exhausted
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no modifier that asks for backtracking, and `preg_*`'s silent `false` on a backtrack limit is a catchable throw here

rules.title: A literal pattern is validated and tiered while checking, and a malformed one is a compile error
Regex syntax is PCRE's with no `u` modifier, and a construct neither engine supports is diagnosed by name
rules.divergesFromPhp: Unicode mode is not a flag because `string` is always UTF-8, and `/e` and its relatives are not reintroduced

rules.title: `echo` in an HTTP request escapes everything it is given, and `Core\Html\Markup` is the only raw-write bypass
rules.divergesFromPhp: output is escaped by the sink rather than by a call the developer remembers, and a runtime-computed string can never become `Markup` through `as`

rules.title: ``html`…` `` is a `Core\Html\Markup` whose segments are trusted and whose holes are escaped
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no template literal in PHP; the nearest thing is `<?= ?>` in an inline-HTML region, and this is that rule available in expression position

rules.title: `Core\Html::escape` answers a `Markup`, so the eager-escape habit stops compiling
rules.divergesFromPhp: `htmlspecialchars`'s replacement does not answer a `string`, so its result cannot be concatenated back into one and double-escaped

rules.title: `Core\Html::toSource` is the one way out of a `Markup`, and it takes a written reason
`Core\Html::sanitize` answers a `Markup` by rebuilding the document, never by filtering it
HTML parses by the WHATWG algorithm onto `Core\Xml`'s own tree, and that parse never fails
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `LIBXML_*` flag matrix and no document class that flips between recovering and throwing — the two front doors are two classes

rules.title: `Core\Xml` is a materialising tree beside a one-window stream, and no operation is available through both
rules.divergesFromPhp: `DOMDocument`, `SimpleXMLElement`, `XMLReader` and the expat callbacks are four vocabularies for one document — there are two here, they share a node family, and they share no operation

rules.title: `Core\Xml` refuses a document type declaration whole and resolves no entity, so XXE and billion-laughs are absent rather than bounded
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `libxml_disable_entity_loader`, no `LIBXML_NOENT` and no entity loader for either to have switched — a `<!DOCTYPE …>` does not parse at all

rules.title: `Core\Validate` carries no predicate that names a type, because `as ?T` already is one
rules.divergesFromPhp: `is_numeric`, `ctype_digit`, `filter_var(FILTER_VALIDATE_INT)` and their kind have no replacement — the conversion is the test

rules.title: `Core\Secret::reveal` is the one named way out of `secret`, and it carries a written reason
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no generic unwrap; a confidential value leaves its qualifier only through this member or through a function that consumes it and returns something else

rules.title: `Core\Reflect` is read-only structural introspection, and it is a first-class feature rather than an extension
rules.divergesFromPhp: reflection is always present rather than a compiled-in extension, it covers no traits because there are none, and it never widens access

rules.title: `Core\Ast` runs the compiler's own parser and hands back typed, inert nodes
rules.divergesFromPhp: `token_get_all`'s untyped arrays are replaced by one type per production, and there is no `eval` for a rewritten tree to reach

rules.title: `Core\Topic` is the only way two connections meet, and a slow subscriber is closed rather than tolerated
`Core\Db` is the only database API, and every statement it runs is prepared
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no PDO, no mysqli, no pgsql and no sqlite3 twin, no `quote`/`real_escape_string`, no emulated prepares and no multi-statement query

rules.title: A connection is named in configuration or built from settings, and both memoize for the request
rules.divergesFromPhp: a credential is never a DSN string in program source, and there is no destructor to close a connection — the request teardown does it

rules.title: Three deny-by-default capabilities gate naming a database, dialling one, and issuing DDL to it
rules.divergesFromPhp: opening a connection is a granted act rather than a library call, and a hostname reaching `Settings.host` may not be `tainted`

rules.title: Three connection defaults close holes PHP leaves open, and none can be configured to the unsafe value
rules.divergesFromPhp: `LOCAL INFILE` cannot be enabled, TLS verifies fully rather than `prefer`, and the charset is forced to UTF-8

rules.title: The five drivers are an enum with one `match` per entry point, not a `Driver` trait
A Unix-socket host is the string that deployment already holds, and MSSQL refuses one
`serverVersion` answers what the server said during the handshake, and never spends a round trip
Busy state is a field on the connection, and a wire not at a message boundary is closed rather than reset
Five members run a statement, results are buffered by default, and only one of them streams
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no unbuffered-query flag and no per-driver difference in what a second statement on a busy connection does

rules.title: One placeholder is one value, and expanding a list into `IN` is written with `Core\Db::inList`
rules.divergesFromPhp: an array bound to a placeholder is one value rather than a silently expanded list, and an empty `inList` throws instead of guessing

rules.title: A literal query is checked while compiling, and no vendor's SQL grammar is ever parsed
Every column has one natural Novis type, and the requested type converts losslessly or throws
rules.divergesFromPhp: nothing is a string because the text protocol made it one — a `DECIMAL` is a `decimal`, a `BIGINT UNSIGNED` is a `uint`, and `TINYINT(1)` holding `7` refuses to read as `bool`

rules.title: A streaming result holds its connection until it is drained, and a second statement on it throws
A stream's read state is parked on the connection on every driver, and a buffer is never the answer
A transaction is a closure, and `Transaction` is a `Queryable` rather than a second query surface
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `beginTransaction`/`commit`/`rollBack` on the connection and no `inTransaction`; nesting is a savepoint, and a rollback signal survives an intervening `catch (Throwable)`

rules.title: One `DbError` carries a normalised kind across every driver, and never a bound parameter
rules.divergesFromPhp: an application branches on `ErrorKind::UniqueViolation` rather than on `1062`, `23505` or the text `"Duplicate entry"`

rules.title: The wire lives in `nvs-db` below the standard library, where a codec is borrowed and a state machine is written
A schema is a value with three spellings, and its array form is the canonical one
The schema vocabulary is five constructs shared by all five backends, with no raw escape hatch
A unique key reads nulls as distinct on every backend, and SQL Server spells that as a filtered index
A plan is the difference between a schema value and a live database, and `Core` knows no migrations
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no version number, no history table, no `up`/`down` pair and no fleet lock — the plan is recomputed from the database every time

rules.title: An existing database is read by catalog query, and no DDL parser exists at any tier
Every plan step carries a grade and its complete SQL, and an unknown grade grades up
Something in the database and not in the schema value is reported with its SQL, and never dropped
Planning is an ordinary read, and applying takes `db.schema` under a member named for its risk
One written attribute per format generates a codec, and it is matched by resolved name
rules.divergesFromPhp: no class is serialisable by being a class — a wire format is opted into at the declaration, and visibility never decides what is encoded

rules.title: The field list is the declared property list, and every field is a constructor parameter of the same name
A generated decoder reports every failed field at once, before the constructor runs
rules.divergesFromPhp: a decode failure is one throw carrying a located list, not the first problem the parser happened to hit

rules.title: The derive generates only the half the class does not write, at compile time, storing nothing per object
The job queue is two tables in a connection the operator names, converged by an explicit command
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no broker, no daemon of its own and no implicit boot-time DDL — the tables are created by `nvs queue migrate` and by nothing else

rules.title: A session is opened by calling `Core\Session::start`, and there is no ambient session array
rules.divergesFromPhp: `$_SESSION` does not exist, nothing starts a session implicitly, and a member called before `start` throws

rules.title: `consume` and `shed` are two jobs with two verbs, and neither is a tier of the other
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no per-IP or per-path limiting, no `[ratelimit]` config block and no middleware writing a `429` for you

rules.title: Both tiers run GCRA over one stored timestamp per key, and the `Decision` computes `retryAfter`
An unreachable shared store throws, because whether to fail open is knowledge only the call site has
`Core\Crypto`'s algorithm roster is closed, every algorithm argument is required, and the sealed layout is what a browser reads
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no cipher name in a string and no unauthenticated mode to reach for, so `aes-256-ecb` has no spelling

rules.title: `Core\Signature` signs a canonicalized payload, and the lifetime rides inside the signed bytes
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no string to assemble and therefore nothing for two sides to disagree about, and a verified payload comes back `tainted`

rules.title: `Core\Router` signs a route name and its parameters, so a signature survives a remount
`Core\Uri` spends the omitted-versus-null distinction on three components and on one query parameter at a time
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `parse_url`/`http_build_query` round trip to lose a component in — removing one is a written `null`, and an empty query is a different value from no query

rules.title: A member whose output scales with its input either allocates through the guarded value allocator or bounds the input
Every decompression runs under an output ceiling and a ratio, and there is no spelling for turning either off
rules.divergesFromPhp: `$max_length` was optional and defaulted to unlimited, so the safe call was the one the caller had to remember to write

rules.title: An image is an immutable value carrying a plan, and nothing decodes until a terminal runs it
rules.divergesFromPhp: gd's mutable resource and its ambient mode flags are gone; an operation answers a new value, and the component's entry points are coarse by rule

rules.title: Pixels are RGBA8 and nothing else, which retires gd's palettes, mode flags and drawing primitives
rules.divergesFromPhp: there are no palette images, no `imagesetpixel`, no drawing primitives and no `imageaffine` — four named transforms cover the affine cases a web application reaches for

rules.title: The format roster is a closed table of decoders and encoders, each naming what implements it
rules.divergesFromPhp: TIFF, BMP, TGA, ICO, PNM, HEIC and gd's own formats are not readable at all, and JPEG XL decodes without encoding

rules.title: The pixel cap is read off the header before a buffer is allocated, and a call may only lower it
rules.divergesFromPhp: a decompression bomb is refused from its declared dimensions rather than discovered by exhausting memory

rules.title: `open` orients and converts to sRGB, and `encode` strips metadata unless the plan kept it
rules.divergesFromPhp: a phone photo is upright and a CMYK JPEG is sRGB without the caller knowing the tags exist, and location data does not survive a re-encode

rules.title: Comparison, hashing, placeholders, text, QR codes and SVG are one entry point each, because each is one job
PDF generation is a first-party extension that performs no I/O, and an unresolved asset throws
rules.divergesFromPhp: the SSRF and local-file-read class that defines PHP's HTML-to-PDF libraries is absent by construction — there is nothing in the sandbox to fetch with

rules.title: The only input language is HTML plus a CSS subset, and every backend answers that one interface
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no second FPDF-shaped imperative engine with its own coordinate model — drawings are inline SVG

rules.title: The CSS subset is documented, and the render result lists every declaration it dropped
The writer emits nothing a reader would execute, and equal input gives byte-equal output
A PDF page is a decode-only format of the image component: one page per `open`, priced by the pixel cap
rules.divergesFromPhp: rasterising a page needs no Imagick, no Ghostscript and no shell — it is `Image::open` with a `page` and a `dpi`

rules.title: An encrypted document and a detectable omission both throw, and everything past rasterising is somebody else's job
The spreadsheet component is a first-party extension that fetches nothing and executes nothing it reads
rules.divergesFromPhp: an external workbook reference, a linked image and a remote data connection come back as data, and VBA is enumerable payload that never runs

rules.title: Only an explicit `Formula` value writes a formula cell, so an export built from user data is inert
rules.divergesFromPhp: a string beginning `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` writes as text, so formula injection is closed by type rather than by a remembered quote prefix

rules.title: A workbook crosses the boundary in whole blocks, and a bomb is refused before a sheet buffer exists
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no per-cell accessor to loop over, which is the shape most PhpSpreadsheet code takes

rules.title: The roster is read-wide and write-narrow, a macro is never written, and evaluation is an explicit call
The writer embeds no executable content and no entropy, so equal input gives byte-equal output
`Core\Net` is one class over TCP, UDP and Unix sockets, reached through five entry points that park on the runtime's own reactor
A `Core\Net` socket closes with the request that opened it, so there is no persistent connection and no pool across requests
A datagram socket sends and receives messages and offers no ordering, retransmission or acknowledgement above them
